rulings.raw: 3 to 3 ½ pounds Boneless Eye of Round Roast
rulings.evidence: Agrees with the estate's own prior ruling of this exact phrase (2026-08-26). The board carries no commodity for it, so the id is new and goes to the registrar; 1474 g (3.25 lb midpoint) over 8 servings reproduces the source's published 40 g protein almost exactly (39.5 g), which is the check that matters on the main protein.

rulings.raw: 2 tsp Chopped Fresh Thyme ((substitute: 1 tsp Dried))
rulings.evidence: 'Chopped' is a prep word, so this is a RENAME onto the same food as the recipe's other thyme line, not a new item. REFUSED the dried-thyme bridge the near-miss row offers: dried is a different price class and about a third of the gram weight. fresh-thyme is already a live board id (4 of 7), so this is a reuse, not a proposal.
Board-live fresh-thyme (4 of 7, cheapest 3.18 at Aldi) and the shelf's own 'fresh thyme -> fresh-thyme' ruling of 2026-08-26, whose 1 g per sprig I adopt for 4 sprigs. No bridge to dried-thyme.

Exactly parallel to the vocabulary's existing 'Dry White Wine -> white-wine' row: 'dry' is a style word on the same food, and red-wine is board-live (4 of 7, cheapest 0.2358 at Baker's), so this is a reuse. Explicitly NOT red-wine-vinegar, a standing form-flip rejection. 1 cup of wine = 236 g.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: The pre-resolve board check reports ABSENT across the commodity namespaces and the captures for this id, and no vocabulary row shares a core word with the name. Eye of round is a distinct whole-muscle lean roast from the round primal: it is not ground beef, not stew beef, not chuck roast and not any steak cut already on the board, so no existing id prices this food under another spelling - the near-miss shelf returned only chicken and pork boneless-cut rulings, which is what an unpriced beef cut looks like. It carries its own price class (a lean, cheap roasting cut sold whole) and its own gram basis, so bridging it to any existing beef id would publish a wrong price on the recipe's main protein. Requesting a new id, not an alias.
